title: The pro-étale site is subcanonical and its sheaves form a topos
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ its small pro-étale site
[def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site].

1. The pro-étale coverings [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] of objects of
   $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ satisfy the axioms of a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: isomorphisms are coverings; if
   $\{U_i\to U\}$ is a covering and $\{U_{ij}\to U_i\}$ are coverings, then
   $\{U_{ij}\to U\}$ is a covering; if $\{U_i\to U\}$ is a covering and $V\to U$ is a
   morphism of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, then the fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] exist in
   $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $\{U_i\times_UV\to V\}$ is a covering.
2. For every object $T$ of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ the representable presheaf
   $h_T=\Hom_X(-,T)$ is a sheaf; that is, the topology is subcanonical.
3. $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is essentially small in the larger universe $\mathcal V$ fixed by
   [def-weil-size-convention], and its category $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}};\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V})$ of sheaves of
   $\mathcal V$-sets for its Grothendieck topology admits a $\mathcal V$-small-site
   presentation; equivalently, it is a $\mathcal V$-Grothendieck topos [def-weil-pbc-topos].

proof.text: For the covering axioms use the full category of weakly etale $X$-schemes of the fixed size [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site]. A pro-etale covering has weakly etale members and is fpqc [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. The fpqc components of all three axioms are [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms]. For a singleton isomorphism between objects, the map is weakly etale because every $X$-morphism between weakly etale $X$-schemes is weakly etale [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]. For a composite family, its members are weakly etale by composition stability in the same statement [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]. For a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and $V\to U$, form the scheme fibre products $W_i=U_i\times_U V$ [def-pc-fibre-product], within the fixed scheme universe. The maps $W_i\to V$ are weakly etale by base-change stability, and $W_i\to X$ is weakly etale by composition stability, both from [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability], since $V\to X$ is an object of the site. Thus $W_i\to X$ is again an object. Fullness over $X$ makes the scheme universal property the universal property in this category: the induced map to $W_i$ is over $X$ because either projection gives its prescribed structure map to $X$. The fpqc pullback family from the covering-axioms node therefore is a pro-etale covering. This proves all three axioms.

proof.text: Let $\{U_i\to U\}$ cover and let $a_i:U_i\to T$ be $X$-morphisms agreeing on $U_i\times_U U_j$. The cover is fpqc by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. The compatible-family statement [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] supplies a unique scheme morphism $a:U\to T$ restricting to the $a_i$. Its composite with $T\to X$ and the structure map $U\to X$ restrict to the same map on every $U_i$, since the $a_i$ are over $X$. The uniqueness clause of the same descent statement, now with target $X$, equates these two maps, proving that $a$ is over $X$. Its uniqueness follows from uniqueness as a scheme morphism. This is exactly the equalizer sheaf condition of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] for $\operatorname{Hom}_X(-,T)$, including the empty covering case.

The size convention [def-weil-size-convention], explicitly used by [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site], fixes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ and a $\mathcal V$-small skeleton within the chosen bound. Thus essential smallness here is relative to $\mathcal V$, not a claim of $\mathcal U$-essential smallness. Write $e:\mathcal D\to X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ for the equivalence from that skeleton and $J$ for the topology established in step 1. The induced-topology statement [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-sheaf-transport] gives a Grothendieck topology $K$ on $\mathcal D$ and an equivalence $e^*:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},J;\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D,K;\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V})$. Its hypotheses hold: $e$ is an equivalence, and $K$ is defined to be its induced topology. This is the small-site presentation, rather than an identification of the two sheaf categories by equality.

source.place: Proof paragraph *3*, first sentence; Stacks Sites Tag 03A0, lemma-equivalence, for sheaf transport

proof.text: By step 3, $\mathcal D$ is a skeleton chosen within the bound of [def-weil-size-convention], so its objects and morphisms form sets in $\mathcal V$; $K$ is a Grothendieck topology on $\mathcal D$; and $e^*:\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proet}},J;\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V})\simeq\Sh(\mathcal D,K;\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V})$ is an equivalence of categories. These are exactly the data of a $\mathcal V$-small-site presentation in [def-weil-pbc-topos], so $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proet}};\operatorname{Sets}_{\mathcal V})$ is a $\mathcal V$-Grothendieck topos. With this definition (Stacks 00XA: a topos is the category of sheaves on a site, up to equivalence) the blueprint's alternative description by Giraud's theorem or as a left exact reflective subcategory of presheaves is not needed.
